name: India–Pakistan
value: Indus treaty suspended; no new LoC strike
summary: India keeps the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance; Pakistan names a minister for an SCO meeting in New Delhi on 15 Nov
state: India continues to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, and Pakistan's leaders have warned that diverting its water would be treated as an act of war (Dawn). The most recent border incident found was the killing of two civilians near the Kasur border on 2 Oct, for which Pakistan summoned India's envoy. On 15 Nov Pakistan's Foreign Office said Climate Minister Musadik Malik would represent it at an SCO meeting in New Delhi (Dawn). No cross-border strike or mobilisation was found as of 15 Nov; ongoing treaty suspensions keep Watch.
for_you: Travellers to the Line of Control and border areas face the most risk; check FCDO travel advice for India and Pakistan. Farmers and cities that depend on the Indus river system are most exposed to any change in water flows.
rubric_hit: Watch: treaty suspension in force (Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance); no cross-border strike or mobilisation
